items.title: New monolithic ion trap opens quantum simulations to more researchers
items.abstract: Some quantum systems are so complex that even the most powerful supercomputers struggle to simulate their behavior. One solution is quantum simulation: building a controllable quantum system in the lab and tuning it to mimic the one researchers want to understand.

items.title: Scientists who discovered a third form of magnetism win major physics prize
items.abstract: Physicists have uncovered a hidden third form of magnetism that challenges more than 100 years of established physics. Called altermagnetism, the discovery could transform future computing and electronics while opening an entirely new frontier in quantum research.

items.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test
items.abstract: Qubits, the quantum equivalent of digital bits, are fragile and prone to errors. That makes building reliable quantum computers extremely difficult. One fix has been to use traditional magic state distillation, which filters out flaws, but it is extremely resource-intensive.

items.title: Infrared light overcomes mirror coating obstacle in gravitational wave detector upgrades
items.abstract: Researchers have developed and tested a new locking method for gravitational wave detectors that will advance the discovery of distant black holes and neutron stars colliding.
